disclaimer: Every item carries its price with a source and a declared PROVENANCE, which is what separates a number from a guess: paid means somebody paid it and there is a record; market means what the thing is worth on a given date, and it will change tomorrow; estimate means someone else’s arithmetic that the owner of the number never confirmed, and it always comes with the name of whoever estimated it. No price here is our own calculation.
caveat: One limit that has to be said with the same weight as the number: this page compares one year of revenue with the cost of BUYING a thing, and buying is not running. A school needs a teacher every month; a hospital needs doctors and medicine; a submarine needs a crew. Swapping tax for any of these lists would not be public policy — it is arithmetic, and it serves exactly one purpose: to give size to a number nobody can picture on their own.
fx.note: Prices in dollars and euros are converted at the Central Bank’s selling PTAX rate of 21 August 2026, historical prices included. It is today’s conversion of yesterday’s price — good for scale, not for reconstructing what it would have cost at the time.
families.social: What the state would buy from itself
families.brasil: What Brazil has already paid for
items[0].label: the 11,469 stalled public works
items[0].detail: The Federal Audit Court's own survey, April 2025: of the 22,621 federal works under way, 11,469 were stalled — one in every two. R$ 15.9 billion has already been spent on them. Education and health account for 70% of the stoppages.
items[1].label: the whole 2014 World Cup
items[1].detail: Final bill consolidated by the Federal Audit Court: R$ 25.5 billion. R$ 8 billion on stadiums, R$ 7 billion on urban mobility, R$ 6.2 billion on airports.
items[2].label: the Abreu e Lima refinery
items[2].detail: Announced at US$ 2.5 billion, it cost US$ 18 billion. Both figures came from Petrobras’s own former chief executive, Graça Foster, testifying to the congressional inquiry: according to the Chamber of Deputies news agency, she said the company made a mistake when it announced the initial figure, and that the gap came from the lack of a reliable basic design. In her words: "A previsão inicial correta seria um custo de cerca de 14 bilhões de dólares".
items[3].label: the Navy's submarine programme
items[3].detail: ProSub — four conventional submarines, one nuclear, a base in Itaguaí and a shipyard. In absolute terms it is the largest military technology programme of the Brazilian armed forces.
items[4].label: finishing the Angra 3 nuclear plant
items[4].detail: The site has been idle since 2015 and has already swallowed nearly R$ 12 billion. Finishing it would cost another R$ 25 billion; abandoning it would cost R$ 21 billion. While nobody decides, keeping the works frozen costs R$ 1 billion a year.
items[5].label: the Transnordestina railway
items[5].detail: Work began in 2006. Twenty years on: R$ 7 billion spent, four of the eleven stretches never started, and a total budget now at R$ 15 billion — 233% above the original figure.
items[6].label: the Mané Garrincha stadium
items[6].detail: Budgeted at R$ 696,648,486.09 and delivered at R$ 1,978,265,062.10 — almost three times the estimate, according to the final audit by the Federal District Audit Court. It is the most expensive stadium of the 2014 World Cup.
items[7].label: the Maracanã refurbishment
items[7].detail: The budget went from R$ 700 million to R$ 1.2 billion. Exame reported that the Rio de Janeiro State Audit Court’s audit found R$ 211 million above the reference price.
items[8].label: all of Petrobras
items[8].detail: Market value of Latin America's largest company in February 2026. A listed company: the number changes every day.
items[9].label: the Arena da Amazônia
items[9].detail: Budgeted at R$ 580 million and delivered at R$ 660 million, in Manaus, for four World Cup matches. No major club in the city plays there. In 2021, with the health system of Amazonas collapsing, the state government was spending around R$ 1 million a month to keep the stadium empty.
items[10].label: the bullet train that never left the drawing board
items[10].detail: The Rio–São Paulo–Campinas high-speed line was budgeted by the government at R$ 35 billion, due to open in 2019. Three auctions were held and nobody bid: the market put it above R$ 50 billion. Not a metre of track was ever laid.
items[11].label: Twitter
items[11].detail: What Elon Musk paid for the social network in 2022.
items[12].label: all of Disney
items[12].detail: Market value of The Walt Disney Company in August 2026. A listed company: the number changes every day.
items[13].label: the International Space Station
items[13].detail: The most expensive object humanity has ever built: five space agencies, 420 tonnes in orbit, US$ 150 billion counting every country’s contribution and the 36 shuttle flights.
items[14].label: the entire Apollo programme
items[14].detail: Everything it took to put a man on the Moon: US$ 25.4 billion in 1973 dollars — the figure NASA itself submitted in writing to the US Congress. In today’s dollars it would be far more.
items[15].label: the James Webb Space Telescope
items[15].detail: Budgeted at US$ 1 billion, due to launch in 2010. It cost around US$ 10 billion and went up in 2021.
items[16].label: Chelsea Football Club
items[16].detail: The largest sale of a sports club up to that point. Todd Boehly’s consortium paid £4.25 billion — about US$ 5.4 billion — in 2022.
items[17].label: the Burj Khalifa
items[17].detail: The tallest building in the world, in Dubai: six years of construction, US$ 1.5 billion.
items[18].label: GTA VI
items[18].detail: The most expensive game ever made. Rockstar has NEVER disclosed the budget — Take-Two’s chief executive said, without giving a number, that the cost is in the billions. Analyst estimates range from US$ 1 billion to US$ 2 billion, marketing included.
items[19].label: the most expensive painting ever sold
items[19].detail: "Salvator Mundi", attributed to Leonardo da Vinci, hammered down at Christie’s New York on 15 November 2017 for US$ 450.3 million after 19 minutes of bidding. The house had estimated US$ 100 million.
items[20].label: the most expensive car ever sold
items[20].detail: A 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé, one of only two in existence, sold in May 2022 for €135 million. Mercedes-Benz itself announced the price.
items[21].label: Neymar's transfer
items[21].detail: The €222 million Paris Saint-Germain paid Barcelona on 3 August 2017 — the release clause. The previous record was less than half that.
items[22].label: the whole Qatar World Cup
items[22].detail: The most expensive World Cup in history: US$ 220 billion, fifteen times more than any other country has spent to host the tournament — the second most expensive is Brazil’s, in 2014, at US$ 15 billion, and Russia spent US$ 11.6 billion in 2018. Qatar’s government has NEVER confirmed the figure: the US$ 220 billion is an estimate by the press and by analysts.
items[23].label: Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour
items[23].detail: The highest-grossing tour in the history of music: US$ 2,077,618,725 across 149 shows, with 10,168,008 tickets sold. Double the runner-up. Money that ten million people paid out of their own pockets.
items[24].label: the Boston Celtics
items[24].detail: The largest sale of a North American sports team: US$ 6.1 billion in 2025. The previous owners had bought the club for US$ 360 million in 2002 — seventeen times less.
items[25].label: Jeff Bezos’s yacht
items[25].detail: Koru, the largest sailing yacht in the world: 127 metres, three masts, nine cabins and a crew of 36. The US$ 500 million price is what the press reported; neither Bezos nor the Oceanco shipyard has confirmed it.

earth.note: The circumference of the equator comes from π × diameter: approximately 40,074 km. The diameter is NASA’s; the multiplication is ours.
items[26].label: the Tokyo Olympics
items[26].detail: US$ 12.9 billion, according to the Japanese government’s own audit — 20% above what the organising committee had announced. The Board of Audit report added US$ 2.1 billion that was missing from the final accounts and flagged a lack of transparency by both the government and the committee.
items[27].label: the Channel Tunnel
items[27].detail: The GI Hub draft reports a £9.5 billion cost and private financing. Its initial factsheet converts this to US$11.8 billion, used in this comparison; the next page reports US$14.5 billion. This inconsistency in the document prevents treating its dollar conversion as definitive.
items[28].label: Apple’s headquarters
items[28].detail: Apple Park, in Cupertino: the 2.8-million-square-foot ring for 12,000 employees. The US$ 5 billion is a market estimate, land purchase included — Apple has never disclosed the cost. The Steve Jobs Theater alone is said to have cost US$ 179 million.
items[27].source: Global Infrastructure Hub — Channel Tunnel draft study, pp. 1–2
